**CR-9. Write discipline and atomicity.** A block is written only by its owner's mutators, and only inside a `WriteScope` the kernel issues during P2 apply or P3 step; outside those phases a mutator is refused in every build (no write, no dirty key), increments `WRITE_OUTSIDE_SCOPE` and reports a violation (CR-19). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Cross-block commands** (weld, cut, module install, pod hop) call *public mutators* other owners explicitly publish; the kernel guarantees the whole `apply` is atomic against every other command, hook and snapshot, followed by one notification batch. **Failure model: validate-then-apply, no rollback.** `validate` proves everything through read-only queries (for weld, the Graph's pure join-validation query); `apply` is infallible by contract; a failure inside `apply` — reported through the fault channel, never by throwing or asserting (CR-19) — is a defect that moves the kernel to `FAULTED` (C.2). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Copy-on-write rollback rejected for MVP cost; event sourcing rejected as primary store — the kernel keeps a bounded command log for diagnostics and replay tests only.)* Step hooks affect other systems by (a) a published unconditional mutator (a horror writing a footprint into the Graph's footprint channel) or (b) a `SYSTEM`-origin command processed at T+1 when the target may reject. The kernel enforces *phase*; "only declared callers call declared mutators" is enforced by lint and the control manifest. → ADR

**Owner rule for `SYSTEM`-submitting hooks** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. The pending queue is kernel data, not a block, so it is not in a snapshot, and a `SYSTEM` rejection is invisible to hooks (results go to the log only). A hook that submits `SYSTEM` commands (Assembly's `weld` / `seam_cut` completions, Transit's `pod_*`, Horror) must therefore be **restart-safe and rejection-tolerant**: its decision to submit is a function of persisted state, so after a restore (pending queue empty, `Dropped(RELOAD)`) it simply decides again; the completions are idempotent; timeouts are expressed in state (`submit_T + PENDING_TTL_TICKS + 1`), never as 'wait for the result'. A divisor-1 hook must guard re-submission with `has_pending(type, dedupe_key)` (or a `dedupe_key` on `submit_system`), because while the queue is backlogged it would otherwise queue a duplicate every tick. G4 (CR-13) holds only for owners that obey this rule.

**CR-10. Change notification contract.** Notifications are emitted once per tick in P5, after commit, batched per block as `(block_id, tick, change_keys)`; if more than `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` changed, `change_keys` collapses to `ALL`. **Payloads carry no state**; subscribers fetch through read views, so notifications are identical whether state arrived by command (`HOST`) or by replication (`MIRROR`) and presentation never changes between modes. Subscriber classes are declared at subscribe time:

| Class | May do | Examples |
|-------|--------|----------|
| `PRESENTATION` | Read `SIM` and `PERCEPTION_OUT` views; write only CanvasItem / Material / Light2D / particle / audio nodes | Failure & Trail, Instruments, HUD, Lighting, Perception Filter, Audio |
| `INPUT_SURFACE` | As `PRESENTATION`, plus **submit** commands as the local seat | Player input adapter, Chart Table, menus |
| `PROJECTOR` | Same reads; write engine-side *derived* objects owned by its block owner (physics shapes, bodies, scene content); never writes blocks | Body's Vertical Slice physics shapes (at MVP the Layout's integer footprint rectangles are SIMULATION data read by Body's `LocomotionStep` and the Emitter's segment test; the avatar has no physics body *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from ship-section-and-layout-data-model)*); derelict content build |
| `REPLICATION` | Read views marked for replication; send | Co-op adapter (VS-B) |
| `DIAGNOSTIC` | Read everything, including kernel internals | Debug Overlay |
| *(none for SIM)* | An object that **owns a block or a hook** never subscribes; sim-to-sim is ordered step reads or commands. The rule is per subscriber *object*, not per system: Player Controller's input adapter and Interaction's prompt object are separate objects that subscribe as `INPUT_SURFACE` (they own no block and no hook) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | — |

Subscriber handlers run with writes disabled. Render `PRESENTATION` gets no submit API; `INPUT_SURFACE` is the one class that may submit, which is how "presentation never writes simulation" coexists with menus that issue commands. *(The `INPUT_SURFACE` and `PROJECTOR` readings of the TD rule are provisional pending a technical-director ruling — Open Questions.)* **Sim never calls presentation**: the flow is always state → notification → presentation. Horror light disturbance and Attention flicker are state that Lighting reads, not calls into Lighting. There are two consumer channels: true values (Debug Overlay only) and filtered values (the Perception Filter reads true state and publishes what a client perceives; presentation nodes read the filtered channel). The kernel exposes `tick_alpha` for render interpolation; owners of moving state expose previous and current committed values in their read views. → ADR for transport (signals vs registry). **Catch-up delivery** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; ratified 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions), R-12, Open Question 21 resolved)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: in a frame that runs more than one tick, `PRESENTATION`, `PROJECTOR` and `DIAGNOSTIC` batches are delivered once, after the frame's last tick, with `tick` = that tick and `change_keys` = the union of the frame's ticks (collapsing to `ALL` past `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS`), because presentation only ever reads the last committed state and N intermediate batches are wasted work; `INPUT_SURFACE`, `REPLICATION` and control-plane callers still receive every tick's batch, and the result buffer is flushed every tick. Ticks stay atomic (G6); only the delivery of a presentation batch is merged. **Delivery on an early exit from the loop** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: if the loop stops early (a P6 pause, a restore, a fault), the merged batch covers **committed ticks only** — the union of the `change_keys` of ticks whose P4 ran — and is delivered at the exit, after the state change is visible to the driver; a fault delivers nothing for the faulting tick (P4 never ran) and merges nothing, and a restore delivers `ALL` for every block to every subscriber class (the world was replaced) once the kernel is `RUNNING` again. **Subscriber lifetime** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: `subscribe(class, handler)` returns a **subscription handle**; `handle.unsubscribe()` removes it, and the kernel also checks `handler.is_valid()` before each call and prunes a freed subscriber (counter `DEAD_SUBSCRIBER`, not an error and not `INCOMPLETE`), so a freed HUD or Chart Table node never raises an engine error that would be misreported. P5 iterates a **snapshot of the subscriber list taken before P5 begins**, so a handler that subscribes or unsubscribes during delivery affects the next tick only. `Kernel.dispose()` (idempotent) unsubscribes everything, drops the registries and breaks the `RefCounted` cycles between kernel, driver and handles, so a test kernel is freed deterministically (no leaked instances at test end).

**CR-11. Time model for presentation.** Presentation runs at render rate and reads last-committed state. It never causes a tick; pausing presentation effects (reduced motion) never pauses the sim.

**CR-12. Perception isolation, enforced by block class.** `SIM` blocks are readable by simulation code and presentation. `PERCEPTION_OUT` blocks (Sanity's per-player "what lies to show" output) are *write-only to simulation*: no sim code — including the owner's own hooks — obtains a read view; presentation and the replication adapter do. Sanity's drift and the friendly-harm gate read the sanity *level* (`SIM`), never the perception block. A sim-side read of a `PERCEPTION_OUT` view is refused in every build: it returns an empty view, increments `PERCEPTION_READ_BLOCKED` and reports a violation (CR-19). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* Perception state is `persist = false` by default (rebuilt from the sanity level and the persisted `sanity.ledger`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from sanity-and-hallucination-rules (C19))* and `OWNER_PRIVATE` in VS-B.

**Read views are getter-only facades or copies, and the guarantee is 'structural plus tripwire'** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. GDScript has no const references: a `Dictionary`, `Array` or Packed array returned from a view is a live container any reader could write to. A read view therefore returns either a facade exposing getters only (indexed access into the owner's storage, for large blocks such as the Graph) or a copy (`duplicate_deep()` / `duplicate()`, for small blocks) — never the owner's live container. What the kernel enforces *structurally* is the issuance surface: `WriteScope` exists only in P2/P3, `PRESENTATION` and `PROJECTOR` receive no submit handle, and owners register no subscription. What it can only *detect* is a reader that mutates a container it should not hold: under `STRICT_DEBUG` the kernel hashes the `SIM` blocks (uncached, so a write that bypassed the dirty bit is seen) **once per dispatch batch** (before the batch's first `validate` and after its last — a `validate` that mutated is caught as a changed hash across the batch and named by block, which is coarser than per-command and is the cost trade) **and once around P5**, and a changed hash is a `SIM_WRITE_TRIPWIRE` violation naming the block *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review; the earlier "around each `validate`" cost up to 129 uncached encodes per tick and made the dev profile unplayable during a burst)*. The tripwire is the only detector for a missed dirty mark, so its **coverage may not shrink**: these per-tick hashes run under a wall-clock budget cap (`TRIPWIRE_BUDGET_MS`, dev only, **[PLACEHOLDER]** 1.0 ms per tick; blocks over the cap are deferred, never skipped), and **every `SIM` block is swept at least once every `TRIPWIRE_SWEEP_TICKS` ticks (**[PLACEHOLDER]** 60) wherever the budget deferred it**; the test profile ignores the budget and always hashes uncached around every batch and P5 *(CD resolution of the tripwire disagreement)*. H3/H4 are thus enforced by structure, lint and tripwire together, not by structure alone.

**CR-13. Determinism and ordering guarantees** (`HOST` mode, same build and platform). **G1 Order**: commands apply in ascending `(queued_tick, host_order)`; in single-player that is submission order. *Carve-out (paused service cycle, CR-2)*: commits there are ordered by the same key but at the frozen `T`. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **G2 Single timeline**: every command applies at exactly one tick (a paused-cycle commit applies at the current, frozen `T`; running-tick commands satisfy `apply_tick ≥ queued_tick + 1`). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **G3 Replay**: from an initial snapshot, the same `PLAYER` command stream, the same *recorded physics observations* and the same **control-plane request log** (each request with the boundary at which it was honoured, including any paused cycle's `host_order` keys, the `restore_epoch` each restore or new game installed, and every accepted or refused runtime `set_knob` change with its boundary) yield identical block state at tick N (canonical snapshot hash), **given `(save bytes, restore_epoch)`**: the same pair replays identically and a different epoch changes exactly the epoch-keyed threat streams (D.10) and nothing else *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R1)*. **The log's format and owner**: the kernel emits one diagnostic *request event* per control-plane request and per admitted `PLAYER` command `(kind, boundary = (T, phase or frame-boundary), host_order, payload digest)`; a **test-side recorder** subscribed as `DIAGNOSTIC` collects them into the replay stream. The `COMMAND_LOG_CAPACITY` ring buffer is a diagnostics aid with eviction and is **not** the replay source *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **G4 Save equivalence**: snapshot at T, restore, continue ≡ uninterrupted play for `persist` blocks (hash-compared) — the key regression test for CR-8. *Preconditions*: (1) every `SYSTEM`-submitting hook obeys the CR-9 owner rule (the pending queue is not saved, so a `SYSTEM` command queued at tick T's P3 is absent after a restore at T; a restart-safe hook resubmits from state); (2) **no `PLAYER` command is pending at the capture boundary** — pending commands are not in the snapshot and are `Dropped(RELOAD)` by the restore, so a capture with a non-empty queue is not equivalent to uninterrupted play; the harness captures at a boundary where the queue has drained (it submits nothing on the preceding tick), and the **remaining command stream** is then defined as the recorded `PLAYER` commands admitted **after** that boundary, fed to both runs; (3) the restored run and the control run use the **same `restore_epoch`** (tests pin it; the control run's epoch is the one the restored run was given), because a different epoch deliberately changes threat draws *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; re-review, delegated ruling R1)*. **Cross-platform note**: G1–G4 are guaranteed on the same build and platform only; a save written on another platform or build that reports `match = false` in the K-4 verdict is expected where any `SIM` state is float-valued, not a kernel defect, and Save/Load's REBASED policy must treat it so *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. **G5** exactly-one-result (CR-5). **G6 Atomic ticks** (CR-2). Physics-derived facts (positions after collision, contacts, raycasts) are *inputs* from the engine: Godot Physics 2D makes no determinism claim, so G3 either records and replays them or excludes physics-coupled blocks. This is a stated limit, not a defect; host-authoritative co-op needs host truth, not cross-machine lockstep. In the MVP no block is physics-coupled: Body's `body.integrate` hook integrates ship-local integer kinematics and samples nothing (the avatar has no physics body), so G3 needs no recorded observations and Open Question 5 is moot for the MVP *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from ship-body-and-interior-physics (BDY-3))*. → ADR

**CR-14. Hard rules** — each becomes a lint, a test, or a control-manifest line. **H1** No domain state in the kernel (kernel-owned data is exactly: `kernel.clock`, the command queue, the registries, the binding tables, the command log, kernel state, diagnostics). **H2** No kernel-defined domain commands; its control plane (CR-15) is a host-local API, not commands. **H3** One owner per block; writes only via owner mutators inside a `WriteScope`. **H4** Presentation never writes simulation; render presentation has no submit API. **H5** No simulation system reads perception state. **H6** Peer identity on every command, kernel-stamped, never payload-borne; a command constructor without `issuer_peer` must not exist. **H7** Everything crossing the kernel boundary is plain data. **H8** No networking code in MVP: the only ingress is local input, the only egress local presentation. **H9** Simulation never reads wall-clock or global RNG. **H10** Kernel logic is scene-tree independent — runs headless, testable without a scene; a `Kernel.step()` call advances the sim synchronously in tests. Autoload vs node → ADR; if an autoload exists it is a thin holder of an instance that code receives as a parameter, so tests never share global state.

**CR-15. Control plane** (host-local, not commands): `request_pause`, `request_resume`, `request_snapshot`, `request_restore`, `request_new_game` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review; CR-18)*, `request_shutdown`. Callers: Save/Load, the pause/Chart Table UI (host-local call), boot code. **Timing** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: a request is recorded when made — from any phase, from a hook, from a P5 handler, or from outside a tick (a UI call between frames) — and served at the **next boundary**, where a boundary is the P6 of a tick or the driver's per-frame boundary service (run before any tick of the frame and, while `PAUSED`, every frame), whichever comes first; the call itself never changes state. `request_shutdown` is accepted from **every state except `SHUTTING_DOWN`** (including `BOOTING`, `LOADING` and `SAVING`; in those it is served at the boundary that follows the atomic step). Requests reaching the same boundary are applied in arrival order, never coalesced: a `request_pause` then a `request_resume` on one boundary leaves the kernel `RUNNING` with no paused service cycle run; a caller that needs a definite state re-issues the state it wants (Chart Table CT-4) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from chart-table-web-map-and-menus (ASK-CT-9))*. **`request_restore(payload, restore_epoch, expected_state_hash = none)`** (K-4) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R1; amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R1 as amended by R13/R14: `restore_epoch` is supplied by Save/Load, whose epoch staging step has completed before the call is made: `EPOCH_DURABLE`, or a logged `SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE` with `save_status = FAILED`, or no advance was due. Save/Load advances the value on every death-stub restore, every `FAULT_RECOVERY` and every Continue except one of the newest non-demoted verified `QUIT` generation, which carries it unchanged and writes nothing (R13). The kernel never waits on that write: no Save/Load I/O completes inside `LOADING`, which stays atomic within one boundary service (States). **Listed exposure (failure path, R14):** after `SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE` the installed epoch exists only in Save/Load's memory, so a process kill before Save/Load's next successful epoch write may replay that epoch once; G3/G4 are unaffected because they are defined given the `(save bytes, restore_epoch)` pair. The kernel holds it read-only for the session, exposes it in the `kernel.clock` read view (CR-8) and rejects a value outside the u32 range in its pre-check, `RESTORE_EPOCH_RANGE`)*: when an expected hash is given, the kernel recomputes `state_hash(PERSIST, T)` (D.12) after the last `post_restore()`, inside `LOADING` and before the first `RUNNING` tick, and reports `{T, computed_hash, match}` to the requester; Save/Load derives its EXACT / REBASED / mismatch verdict from it (SL-12). A mismatch is **not** a `FAULTED` transition — release plays on; policy is the requester's. Save/Load does not use restore-into-`PAUSED` for this window *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from save-load-and-versioned-format (K-4))*. **Control-plane read access:** a control-plane caller is not one of the CR-10 subscriber classes; Save/Load (the one such caller at MVP) may read `kernel.clock`, the Controller's per-seat `loco_state`, the Graph's `read_view.failures()` and an optional Attention `SIM` read view, and receives end-of-tick notifications, all read in the tick boundary in which it issues a request; it never reads `PERCEPTION_OUT`, never submits commands and never holds a `WriteScope` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from save-load-and-versioned-format (SL-13))*. In VS-B a guest's pause or save *request* is a command defined by Session or Save/Load, validated on the host, which then calls the control API.

**CR-16. Pause semantics.** `PAUSED` stops the tick but not rendering. While paused, submit accepts only types flagged `allowed_when_paused` by their owner, and **only non-diegetic actions may carry the flag** (save, settings, resume, menu navigation) — no gameplay verb that changes `SIM` state is allowed while paused, so a solo player cannot equip, repair or re-route with time stopped mid-tell (Dread Before Chaos), and solo pause behaves like co-op's overlay-only pause; a paused-allowed command may write only blocks registered `gameplay = false` **and** named in the type's `writes_blocks` (boot-checked, CR-6; the `WriteScope` issued in the paused cycle carries exactly that set, and a write outside it is refused and counted as `WRITE_OUTSIDE_SCOPE`), never a `SIM` gameplay block *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; everything else is rejected `PAUSED` immediately, never queued, so there is no burst on resume. Admitted paused-allowed commands are dispatched by a **paused service cycle** that runs P1, P2, P4, P5 and P6 with no P3 and with `T` unchanged, **once per rendered frame while `PAUSED`** (the paused boundary, which also serves control-plane requests), so a save or a menu action takes effect without advancing simulated time. At MVP no command type sets the flag; the cycle is a retained seam that only test fixtures exercise (CR-2). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* Commands already queued when the pause is honoured are neither dispatched by the service cycle nor rejected: they wait, in order, for the first `RUNNING` tick after resume. **Pause is single-player only**: in co-op a menu cannot stop a shared sim — VS-B treats pause as a UI overlay with the kernel `RUNNING`. The Chart Table GDD must not assume "pick a target" happens while paused. Relationship to the scene tree's pause → ADR.

**CR-17. Bounds and overload behaviour.** At most `MAX_CMDS_PER_TICK` processed per tick, the rest waiting FIFO. `QUEUE_CAPACITY` total and `PER_ISSUER_CAPACITY` per issuer; beyond that `QUEUE_FULL` at admission — never silent drop, never unbounded growth. Catch-up runs at most `MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME` ticks per frame, then lets simulated time lag rather than spiral (lag above `LAG_FORGIVE_TICKS` is dropped at the end of the frame, D.5); a lag counter is exposed to diagnostics. P3 exceeding `STEP_BUDGET_MS` logs the slowest hooks but the tick completes. A command older than its type's `max_age_ticks` is rejected `STALE`, so a hitch cannot unleash a second of stale intents. At the defaults `STALE` is unreachable from local ingress (the queue can hold a command at most 8 ticks and `T` does not advance while paused or saving); it is a VS-B seam for remote-stamped ticks, guarded locally by a "never stale" invariant test (Section E; ratified 2026-10-27 — user ruling, R-3). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*

**CR-18. Snapshot semantics.** A snapshot is taken only at a tick boundary (P6), covers all `persist` blocks at the same T, and records `(T, per-block schema_version)`. Capture is synchronous and in memory with the tick halted (`SAVING`), and **atomic within a single boundary service — `SAVING` never spans a frame**; file I/O is Save/Load's and off the critical path → ADR. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* Restore replaces all `WORLD`-scoped persisted blocks atomically and leaves `PROFILE`-scoped blocks untouched (Pillar 5: losing the ship or a body never loses knowledge); partial restore within a scope is unsupported; failure aborts to `FAULTED` with pre-restore state intact where possible. With join-in-progress deferred, the same snapshot/restore contract is VS-B's guest transfer at session start, so it must be complete and cheap. **New game (K-2):** a new game passes through `LOADING`: every block takes `default_state()`, Save/Load's `new_game(world_seed)` sets `world_seed` into `kernel.clock` *(a new game is entered by the control-plane call `request_new_game(world_seed, restore_epoch = 0)`, valid from `BOOTING` (the first boot, States table), `RUNNING`, `PAUSED` and `FAULTED` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*, so a second new game in one process — for example "death = restart from the last autosave" when no autosave exists yet — has a path; it flushes the queue with `Dropped(RELOAD)` exactly like `request_restore`, resets `T` to 0, installs the supplied epoch (a fresh slot's `slot_epoch.bin` starts at 0, Save/Load SL-18, SL-23; amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R14) and leaves `PROFILE`-scoped blocks untouched: Pillar 5, a new world never loses knowledge; what a new crew keeps is Open Question 13, Save/Load's) (Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, then each owner that registered an `init_world(world_seed)` step runs it in `restore_after` order under one `WriteScope`, before `post_restore()`; at MVP the world build is Web Map & Transit's `init_world` (WM-7), which calls the Layout, Graph and Body mutators in its fixed order *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from save-load-and-versioned-format (SL-18) and web-map-and-transit)*. The last step of every pass through `LOADING`, restore or new game, is the CR-7 binding rebuild (after the `init_world` steps and `post_restore()`, and after a restore's K-4 hash check), so the first `RUNNING` tick already sees the rebuilt `PlayerId → {(block_id, entity_id)}` half *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*.

**CR-19. Fault channel, violations and build profiles** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; replaces the earlier 'throws / asserts' model)*. GDScript has no `try`/`catch`: a runtime script error is printed by the engine, aborts the function it occurred in and hands control back to the caller with a default value the caller cannot distinguish from a result; and `assert()` is compiled out of release exports. The kernel therefore **never relies on an exception or an assertion for control flow**, and every behaviour in this document is identical in debug and release unless a clause calls it a `STRICT_DEBUG` extra.
- **(a) Fault channel and the one callable contract** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R3; defines the contract once)*. **Kernel-invoked owner callables** are a closed list: `validate`, `apply`, step hooks, `snapshot`, `restore`, `post_restore`, `default_state`, `read_view`, `commit_baseline`, `snap_baseline`, `init_world`, and the result- and subscriber-handlers. The kernel calls each through `Callable.call()` and passes a context object as the last argument (`ApplyContext`/`WriteScope`, `HookContext`, `SnapshotContext`, `NotifyContext`). **Results flow through `ctx`, never through the return value**: `validate(cmd, views, ctx)` reports through `ctx.ok()` or `ctx.reject(reason)`; `snapshot(ctx)`, `default_state(ctx)` and `read_view(ctx)` deliver their payload through `ctx.put(payload)`; `apply(cmd, write_scope, ctx)`, hooks, `restore`, `post_restore`, `init_world`, `commit_baseline`, `snap_baseline` and handlers report only success-by-completion; every callable reports failure with `ctx.fault(code, detail)`. **Every callable's only return statement is `return ctx.complete()`** (a typed token, (b)); no owner callable is declared `-> void`, because a `void` GDScript function cannot return the token and the engine's default for an aborted typed function would alias a legitimate result. A `validate` that calls neither `ok()` nor `reject()` is `Faulted(NO_OUTCOME)`; the first outcome call stands and a second is a violation (`CTX_DOUBLE_OUTCOME`). **Published mutators are not on this list**: other owners, not the kernel, call them, so the kernel cannot check their sentinel; they take the shared `WriteScope`, report with `scope.fault(code, detail)` and return a status that callers propagate — which is also why the sentinel's blind spot (below) is closed by status propagation. The kernel checks `ctx.faulted` (which includes any fault a mutator reported on the shared scope) and the completion token after **every** kernel-invoked call, before using its result. A fault in `apply`, a hook, `snapshot`, `restore`, `post_restore`, `init_world`, `default_state`, `commit_baseline` or `snap_baseline` (and in a mutator they called) moves the kernel to `FAULTED`; **a fault in `read_view` never does**: views are obtained by presentation at render time, outside any tick, and a HUD read must not be able to halt the ship (CR-11, H4) — it is recorded and counted (`INCOMPLETE` or the violation, as a P5 handler's is), the reader receives an empty view, and when sim code called it inside P2/P3 the enclosing `apply` or hook fails through the status it propagates; a fault reported by `validate` does not reject, it faults (a defect), whereas `ctx.reject(reason)` is the ordinary domain rejection (`Rejected(VALIDATION_FAILED(reason))`, kernel stays `RUNNING`); a fault in a P5 or result handler is recorded and counted but cannot fault the kernel (the tick is committed).
- **(b) Completion sentinel.** The kernel arms `ctx.completed = false` and a fresh `ctx.token` before each call; `ctx.complete()` sets `completed` and returns that token — a typed, non-nil, non-zero object (a per-call `CompletionToken` instance) that the kernel compares **by identity**, so a `null`, `0`, `false` or empty value returned by an aborted or forgetful function can never read as success. A call that returns anything but the armed token with `completed` set (the script aborted on an engine error, or forgot) is `fault(INCOMPLETE)` for `apply`, hooks, `validate`, `snapshot`, `restore`, `post_restore`, `default_state`, `commit_baseline`, `snap_baseline` and `init_world`, and a recorded `INCOMPLETE` diagnostic, without a fault, for a P5 or result handler and for `read_view` (which returns an empty view). In a release build the sentinel is the only abort guard (`assert` is compiled out), so it is exercised on a release export in the spike (Acceptance Criteria, KRN-CTX-06). The sentinel catches a *function that aborted*; it cannot catch an error in a nested helper that the outer function then ignores — which is why mutators also return statuses and callers must propagate them.
- **(c) What cannot be done.** Engine script errors cannot be intercepted. P5 subscriber isolation is therefore **best-effort plus lint**: the kernel calls handlers one at a time from its own loop, so an aborted handler does not stop the loop; the sentinel names the offending subscriber in diagnostics; a lint forbids handlers from calling anything that can write.
- **(d) Violations.** A *violation* (write outside a `WriteScope`, a sim read of `PERCEPTION_OUT`, a hook reaching the `PLAYER` ingress, a submit during `SAVING`, a payload that passed the size check but fails the round-trip, a `SIM` hash change at the tripwire) is, in every build: the offending action refused, a named diagnostics counter incremented, `push_error` called. Under `STRICT_DEBUG` the kernel additionally calls the injected `violation_handler(code, detail)`; the dev default halts via `assert(false)`, the test default records. No state-machine outcome (`FAULTED`, reject reasons, results) differs between profiles.
- **(e) KernelProfile.** `KernelProfile` ∈ {`STRICT_DEBUG`, `LENIENT_RELEASE`} is injected at construction (H10) and never read from `OS.is_debug_build()` inside the kernel, so one test process can construct a kernel per profile and exercise both branches. `STRICT_DEBUG` enables only the extras: the per-command serialization round-trip (CR-4), the violation handler, the `SIM` tripwire (CR-12) and the counter test seams.

**Velocity rule (gameplay-programmer, adopted as an acceptance criterion).** Adding a new command verb touches at most two files: one handler and one registration line. If the kernel ever makes a feature cost more than that, the layer will be bypassed — which is the exact lapse TD-FEASIBILITY named. Hence: commands are plain data records (no class per verb), state blocks are coarse (one per domain system, not per entity), and replay/undo/rollback/middleware are deferred.

752	## Dependencies
753	
754	**Upstream (this system depends on): none.** The kernel is the Foundation layer. It depends on the engine's `_process` callback (through the one `TickDriver` node, CR-1a) and, only if a Vertical Slice physics projection feeds a block, on Godot Physics 2D as a source of *observations* (CR-13); at MVP it depends on no game system and on no physics callback. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
755	
756	**Downstream (systems that depend on this one).** Every row is a registrant: it registers blocks, command types or hooks, or subscribes. Hard = cannot function without the kernel; every registrant and subscriber is hard — a system that could work without the kernel would be writing state outside it, which H3/H4 forbid. The one **Soft** row (the last) is not a registrant: it cites kernel constants and `rng_derive` from static data or through a listed system, and would survive the kernel's absence. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the earlier claim that the kernel had no soft dependents contradicted that Soft row)*

Lost time is **always dropped at the end of the frame, never fast-forwarded**; there is no repay allowance. Replaying a 10–30 s tell window at up to 4× while the player reacts at 1× would compress the tell and read as unfair, so no repayment exists at all; since no domain system reads wall-clock time the drop is observable only in diagnostics. ## Dependencies

**Upstream (this system depends on): none.** The kernel is the Foundation layer. It depends on the engine's `_process` callback (through the one `TickDriver` node, CR-1a) and, only if a Vertical Slice physics projection feeds a block, on Godot Physics 2D as a source of *observations* (CR-13); at MVP it depends on no game system and on no physics callback. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*

**Downstream (systems that depend on this one).** Every row is a registrant: it registers blocks, command types or hooks, or subscribes. Hard = cannot function without the kernel; every registrant and subscriber is hard — a system that could work without the kernel would be writing state outside it, which H3/H4 forbid. The one **Soft** row (the last) is not a registrant: it cites kernel constants and `rng_derive` from static data or through a listed system, and would survive the kernel's absence. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the earlier claim that the kernel had no soft dependents contradicted that Soft row)*

| System | Nature | Interface (kernel side) | Interface (consumer side) | In systems index? |
|--------|--------|-------------------------|---------------------------|-------------------|
| Life-Support Graph | Hard | Registry, step hooks, WriteScope, dirty keys | Blocks, propagation hook, published mutators | Yes |
| Save/Load & Versioned Format | Hard | Control plane (`request_snapshot`/`request_restore`), snapshot/restore semantics, `Dropped(RELOAD)` | File format, migrations, death stub | Yes |
| Player Controller & Input | Hard | Submit (as `INPUT_SURFACE`), coalescing, result events, `tick_alpha` | Intent and action command types | Yes |
| Suit & Equipment | Hard | `PER_PLAYER` blocks keyed by PlayerId, ordered step | Vitals/loadout block and commands | Yes |
| Modular Ship Assembly | Hard | Atomic cross-block `apply`, validate-then-apply | Weld/cut/install commands | Yes |
| Ship Body & Interior Physics | Hard | The `body.integrate` step hook (divisor 1, P3), `PROJECTOR` class for a Vertical Slice physics projection; no physics-step alignment (CR-1a) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | Integration hook (samples nothing), projection; binding source `seat_bindings()` for the `LOADING` rebuild (CR-7) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* | Yes |
| Emitter State & Light-Exposure Query | Hard | Registry, pure-read query rules | Emitter block and commands; binding source `beam_bindings()` for the `LOADING` rebuild (CR-7) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* | Yes |
| Web Map & Transit | Hard | Atomic data apply, hook | World block, `pod_hop` | Yes |
| Horror Entities | Hard | Ordered step, RNG streams, `SYSTEM` commands | Entity block, footprint mutator calls | Yes |
| Sanity & Hallucination Rules | Hard | `SIM`/`PERCEPTION_OUT` class isolation | Sanity level + perception blocks, drift hook | Yes |
| Perception Filter | Hard | `PRESENTATION` subscription, filtered channel | Reads only | Yes |
| Debug Overlay (True Values) | Hard | `DIAGNOSTIC` subscription | Reads only | Yes |
| Interaction System | Hard | Submit, domain reason codes, friendly-harm gate order | Verb command types | Yes |
| Attention System | Hard | Registry, step hook (breach state machine) | Attention block, stimulus intake | Yes |
| Ship Section & Layout Data Model | Hard | Registry (layout block), `PROJECTOR`, the published `block_hash` read (D.12) | Layout block schema; reads `block_hash(&"layout.state")` for `layout_hash()` (D.12) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* | Yes |
| Co-op Session & Replication (VS-B) | Hard | `MIRROR` mode, ingress adapter, binding table API, `REPLICATION` class, `scope`/`repl_hint` | Transport, replication | Yes |
| Pixel-Perfect Render Pipeline & Camera | Hard (reads) | `PRESENTATION`/`INPUT_SURFACE` subscription, `tick_alpha`, kernel state, previous/current views | Reads only; never submits | **No — add edge** |
| 2D Lighting & Occlusion | Hard (reads) | `PRESENTATION` subscription, read views | Reads only | **No — add edge** |
| Failure & Trail System | Hard (reads) | `PRESENTATION` subscription, `rng_derive`, `kernel.clock` view | Registers nothing | **No — add edge** |
| HUD & Suit Layer | Hard (reads) | `PRESENTATION` / `INPUT_SURFACE` subscription, result handler | Reads; submits only through `INPUT_SURFACE` | **No — add edge** |
| In-World Instruments & Inspect View | Hard (reads) | `PRESENTATION` / `INPUT_SURFACE` subscription | Reads; submits only through `INPUT_SURFACE` | **No — add edge** |
| Adaptive Audio & Tells | Hard (reads) | `PRESENTATION` subscription | Reads only | **No — add edge** |
| Chart Table (Web Map & Menus) | Hard (reads) | `INPUT_SURFACE` subscription, control plane (`request_pause`) | Submits no command at MVP (CT-27) | **No — add edge** |
| Item & Module Database, Boarding & Salvage, Derelict Authoring | Soft | Cite `rng_derive`, `MAX_PAYLOAD`, `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS`; register no block of their own with the kernel or do so through a listed system | — | No (static data / through listed systems) |

**Bidirectional consistency.** *(Refreshed 2026-10-27 — design review.)* All 25 other MVP GDDs now exist. The systems index lists the kernel as a dependency of Life-Support Graph, Emitter State, Player Controller, Interaction, Suit & Equipment, Ship Section & Layout, Ship Body, Modular Ship Assembly, Web Map & Transit, Attention, Horror Entities, Sanity, Perception Filter, Save/Load and Debug Overlay — so the four edges the first draft asked for (Interaction, Attention, Ship Section & Layout, Perception Filter) are present. The rows marked **No — add edge** above are the presentation consumers (Pixel-Perfect pipeline, Lighting, Failure & Trail, HUD, Instruments, Audio, Chart Table) that read kernel state without listing the kernel in `Depends On`; they are flagged for the next systems-index pass. The index no longer carries a *Life-Support Graph → Save/Load* edge (the Graph row lists only this kernel), consistent with the registry contract that makes it unnecessary. The Item & Module Database is static definitions and needs no kernel edge.

**Data the kernel takes from consumers, and what it refuses.** It takes registrations (frozen at boot), commands (plain data), and subscriptions. It refuses: object references in any payload (H7), domain state in itself (H1), domain command types (H2), reads of `PERCEPTION_OUT` from sim code (H5), and any write outside a `WriteScope` (H3).

## Tuning Knobs

All knobs below are **provisional until the kernel spike**. Every knob traces to a Section D symbol. "Tunability": **set-once** = fixed at project start, changing it is a code/data migration; **boot** = registration data frozen at `BOOTING → LOADING`, changeable between runs; **runtime** = may be changed by a dev console between ticks (honoured at P6) without invalidating any stored value.

**Coupled constraints (boot assertions — each is one acceptance test):**
1. `max_age_ticks(t) ≥ ceil(QUEUE_CAPACITY / MAX_CMDS_PER_TICK)` for every type `t` — "a local command is never STALE" (D.7, option a).
2. `QUEUE_CAPACITY ≥ max_issuers × PER_ISSUER_CAPACITY + SYSTEM_RESERVE` — "one issuer cannot cause global `QUEUE_FULL`" (MVP: `max_issuers = 2`); every safe range in the knob table is stated so that this holds (the ceiling of `PER_ISSUER_CAPACITY` is `floor((QUEUE_CAPACITY − SYSTEM_RESERVE) / max_issuers)`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.
3. `0 ≤ offset_h < divisor_h` and `divisor_h ≥ 1` for every hook (D.2).
4. *(Removed 2026-10-27 — design review: the tick is driven from `_process`, not the physics callback, so there is nothing to match, CR-1a. The number is kept so existing citations of constraints 5 and 6 stay valid.)*
5. `TICK_RATE` in the snapshot header equals the running constant (ratified 2026-10-27 — user ruling, R-9, Section E). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
6. `T`, `seq`, `host_order`, RNG counters are 64-bit (D.14).
7. *(New 2026-10-27 — design review; re-scoped 2026-10-27 — re-review)* Every runtime change to **any** Runtime knob goes through `set_knob(name, value)`, is range-checked and re-validated against every coupled constraint it appears in at the next boundary, and is refused (previous value kept, `KNOB_REFUSED` counter) if it would violate one; every accepted or refused change is written to the G3 control-plane log with its boundary (CR-13), because `REMOTE_RATE_LIMIT` and `RATE_WINDOW_TICKS` change which commands are admitted and so change replay. The knobs that appear in constraints 1, 2 and 5 (`QUEUE_CAPACITY`, `PER_ISSUER_CAPACITY`, `MAX_CMDS_PER_TICK`, `SYSTEM_RESERVE`, `max_age_ticks`, `TICK_RATE`) are all Boot or Set-once, so after the re-review **no Runtime knob is governed by constraints 1, 2 or 5**; constraint 7's remaining force is the range check and the log. (The earlier text implied it guarded runtime changes to those knobs, which are not runtime.)
8. *(New 2026-10-27 — re-review)* `QUEUE_CAPACITY × (MAX_PAYLOAD + 200 B) + COMMAND_LOG_CAPACITY × (MAX_PAYLOAD + 100 B) ≤ COMMAND_MEMORY_BUDGET` — the knob corners cannot boot (4096 × 64 KiB would be 256 MiB). Boot assertion; corner-case boot ACs below.

**Set-once versus runtime, summarised.** Set-once: `TICK_RATE`, `H64`/`mix64`. Changing `TICK_RATE` after any data file or save exists requires rescaling every tick-expressed value by `new/old` and invalidates every existing save; treat it as a project-start decision confirmed by the kernel spike. Boot-frozen (registration data; change between runs, never mid-session): divisors, offsets, `max_age_ticks`, `MAX_PAYLOAD`, `MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME`, `COMMAND_LOG_CAPACITY`, `MAX_BLOCKS`, `MAX_CMDS_PER_TICK`, `QUEUE_CAPACITY`, `PER_ISSUER_CAPACITY`, `SYSTEM_RESERVE`, `COMMAND_MEMORY_BUDGET`. Runtime (dev console, honoured at the next boundary, no stored value depends on them, constraint 7 applies): `REMOTE_RATE_LIMIT`, `RATE_WINDOW_TICKS`, `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS`, `LAG_FORGIVE_TICKS`, `STEP_BUDGET_MS`, `FRAME_SIM_BUDGET_MS`, `SNAPSHOT_BUDGET_MS`, `DIAG_HASH_CADENCE_TICKS`, `TRIPWIRE_BUDGET_MS`, `TRIPWIRE_SWEEP_TICKS`. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; re-review: `SYSTEM_RESERVE` moved to Boot, new knobs added)*

> **Ruled (user ruling, design-review decisions, 2026-10-27; replaces the CD-GDD-ALIGN 2026-10-25 note's 30-tick starting value and matches D.5)**: `LAG_FORGIVE_TICKS = 0`. Lost time is **always dropped at the end of the frame, never fast-forwarded**; there is no repay allowance. Replaying a 10–30 s tell window at up to 4× while the player reacts at 1× would compress the tell and read as unfair, so no repayment exists at all; since no domain system reads wall-clock time the drop is observable only in diagnostics. The creative-director note ('lost time is never fast-forwarded') is now literally true. `allowed_when_paused` is restricted to non-diegetic actions (CR-16), so the equip-while-paused edge case above resolves as `Rejected(PAUSED)`. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*

| TR-cmd-002 | A `TickDriver` (RefCounted, no scene tree) owns an integer accumulator in microseconds x TICK_RATE (TICK_UNITS = 1,000,000 per tick), is driven from exactly one PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS node's `_process`, and runs at most MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME (4) ticks per frame; the physics step is never the clock. | Threading/Timing | CR-1a, D.5 |
| TR-cmd-003 | Lost time is dropped at end of frame and never fast-forwarded (LAG_FORGIVE_TICKS = 0); the accumulator is cleared on every transition into RUNNING and re-reads kernel state after each `step()`. | Threading/Timing | CR-1a, Tuning Knobs (LAG_FORGIVE_TICKS) |
| TR-cmd-004 | Per-frame order is fixed by process priority: input adapter (0), TickDriver (1: boundary service, tick loop, forgiveness, result flush, paused service), presentation nodes (2), with a lint on process_priority values. | Threading/Timing | CR-1a Step 0 priority table, KRN-LAT-02 |
| TR-cmd-005 | Kernel, driver, and every owner callable run on the main thread only; no Thread, WorkerThreadPool, or call_deferred into kernel code (lint-enforced). | Threading/Timing | CR-1a Main thread |

| TR-cmd-007 | Step hooks register (hook_id, owner, divisor, offset, after[]); the kernel topologically sorts them (ties by registration order then hook_id), a cycle or unknown id fails boot, and an `after` edge across non-coinciding hooks must declare `tolerates_stale`. | Core | CR-3, Tuning Knobs (divisor/offset) |

| TR-cmd-009 | `submit()` is fire-and-forget (returns nothing, calls nothing); each command yields exactly one terminal result record (Applied/Rejected/Dropped/Faulted/Superseded) buffered and flushed at P5 and once per rendered frame in every kernel state; results carry reason codes, never display strings. | Core | CR-5, G5 |

| TR-cmd-017 | Snapshots are taken only at a tick boundary (P6), synchronously in memory in SAVING (atomic within one boundary service, never spanning a frame), cover all persist WORLD blocks at the same T, and restore replaces WORLD blocks atomically while leaving PROFILE blocks untouched. | Save/Load | CR-18, States |
| TR-cmd-018 | `kernel.clock` (T, world_seed) is the kernel's only registered block (SIM, persist, WORLD, never dirty); `restore_epoch` is owned and persisted by Save/Load (`slot_epoch.bin`), passed into `request_restore`/`request_new_game`, held read-only, exposed in the clock read view, and excluded from the snapshot header and all hashes. | Save/Load | CR-8, CR-15, D.10 |
| TR-cmd-019 | RNG is never global: each system draws from a named stream (counter in its block) via the kernel's pure `rng_derive(world_seed, stream_name, counter)` (and `rng_derive_epoch` for threat draws) using SplitMix64 mix64, pinned by golden vectors. | Core | CR-8, D.10, H9 |

| TR-cmd-027 | Commands apply in ascending (queued_tick, host_order) with apply_tick >= queued_tick + 1 while running; from an initial snapshot, same PLAYER command stream plus control-plane request log and same (save bytes, restore_epoch) yields identical canonical hash at tick N on the same build and platform. | Core | CR-13 G1-G4 |

| TR-cmd-030 | Pause is single-player only; while PAUSED only `allowed_when_paused` types (non-diegetic, writing only gameplay=false blocks named in `writes_blocks`) are dispatched via a paused service cycle (P1,P2,P4,P5,P6; no P3; T frozen), and all others are rejected PAUSED without queuing. | Core | CR-16 |
| TR-cmd-031 | Queue bounds are boot assertions: MAX_CMDS_PER_TICK 128, QUEUE_CAPACITY 1024, PER_ISSUER_CAPACITY 256, `max_age_ticks(t) >= ceil(QUEUE_CAPACITY / MAX_CMDS_PER_TICK)`, and QUEUE_CAPACITY*(MAX_PAYLOAD+200B)+COMMAND_LOG_CAPACITY*(MAX_PAYLOAD+100B) <= COMMAND_MEMORY_BUDGET (16 MiB); overflow is QUEUE_FULL, never silent drop. | Performance | CR-17, Tuning Knobs constraints 1, 2, 8 |

| TR-cmd-033 | The kernel is scene-tree independent (headless-testable, `Kernel.step()` synchronous), with KernelProfile (STRICT_DEBUG / LENIENT_RELEASE) injected at construction and never read from `OS.is_debug_build()`; no networking code at MVP (host-only ingress is local input). | Core | CR-14 H8/H10, CR-19(e) |
| TR-cmd-034 | Mode HOST ticks and applies authoritatively while MIRROR applies nothing, with an identical public API; blocks declare `repl_hint` (HOST_ONLY/SHARED_SUMMARY/OWNER_PRIVATE) now though unused until VS-B. | Networking | CR-7, CR-8 (repl_hint), Vocabulary |

- Kernel: `step()`, `Kernel.dispose()`, `tick_alpha`, `T` (tick counter), `Mode` {HOST, MIRROR}, `KernelProfile` {STRICT_DEBUG, LENIENT_RELEASE}
- `TickDriver` (RefCounted; injected `delta_us`); `TICK_RATE`, `TICK_UNITS`
- Command ingress: `submit(type, payload, actor = none, correlation = 0)` on an INPUT_SURFACE handle; `submit_system(type, payload, dedupe_key = none)`; `has_pending(type, dedupe_key)`

- RNG helpers: `rng_derive(world_seed, stream_name, counter)`, `rng_derive_epoch`, `mix64`, `H64`

- Kernel states BOOTING, LOADING, RUNNING, PAUSED, SAVING, FAULTED, SHUTTING_DOWN
- Tuning knobs: TICK_RATE, MAX_CMDS_PER_TICK, QUEUE_CAPACITY, PER_ISSUER_CAPACITY, SYSTEM_RESERVE, MAX_PAYLOAD, MAX_DIRTY_KEYS, MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME, LAG_FORGIVE_TICKS, STEP_BUDGET_MS, FRAME_SIM_BUDGET_MS, SNAPSHOT_BUDGET_MS, DIAG_HASH_CADENCE_TICKS, COMMAND_LOG_CAPACITY, MAX_BLOCKS, COMMAND_MEMORY_BUDGET, REMOTE_RATE_LIMIT, RATE_WINDOW_TICKS, TRIPWIRE_BUDGET_MS, TRIPWIRE_SWEEP_TICKS, PAYLOAD_MAX_DEPTH, MAX_AGE_TICKS_INTENT (30), MAX_AGE_TICKS_ACTION (120), PENDING_TTL_TICKS

## Consumes

- Engine `_process(delta)` via the single TickDriver node (only wall-clock read, plus diagnostics timer); optional Godot Physics 2D observations in Vertical Slice (as inputs, PROJECTOR)
- Save/Load & Versioned Format: supplies `restore_epoch` (`slot_epoch.bin`), calls control plane, owns file I/O and `hex64`; kernel has no upstream game-system dependencies
- Owner-published callables from registrants: Life-Support Graph (`graph.state`, chained propagate hooks, pure join-validation query, `read_view.failures()`), Ship Body (`body.state`, `body.integrate` hook, `seat_bindings()`), Emitter State (`emitter.state`, `beam_bindings()`), Ship Section & Layout (`layout.state`, `block_hash(&"layout.state")`), Web Map & Transit (`init_world`, `pod_*` commands), Suit, Attention, Horror, Sanity (SIM level vs PERCEPTION_OUT), Modular Ship Assembly, Interaction, Player Controller (`loco_state`)
- Consumers that subscribe: Perception Filter, Debug Overlay, HUD, Lighting, Failure & Trail, Instruments, Adaptive Audio, Chart Table, Pixel-Perfect pipeline (read-only except INPUT_SURFACE submitters)

## Engine risk

- `Node._process` ordering, `process_priority`, `PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS` between nodes: LOW (reference silent on cross-node ordering; GDD says verify in spike, KRN-LAT-02)
- `Engine.time_scale` effect on `_process(delta)`: LOW but flagged [UNV] in GDD; verify in spike
- `Callable.call()` with typed return and completion-token identity pattern (GDScript has no try/catch; `assert` compiled out in release): LOW (older), must be exercised on release export (KRN-CTX-06)
- `var_to_bytes(..., false)` / `bytes_to_var` round-trip, Packed*Array pass-by-reference, `duplicate_deep()`: MEDIUM (`duplicate_deep` is 4.5+: HIGH)
- 4.7 behavior change: writing one element of a packed array no longer fires the property setter, so dirty tracking must be explicit in mutators: HIGH
- `HashingContext` SHA-256 over raw Packed bytes (H64): LOW
- `RefCounted` cycle breaking / deterministic free in tests; typed GDScript classes (no `-> void` on kernel callables): LOW
- Godot Physics 2D (no determinism claim; VS projection only, not MVP): LOW (Jolt default is 3D only)
- MultiplayerAPI / peer_id semantics (VS-B, MIRROR mode, no networking at MVP): MEDIUM, dormant

- `RefCounted` cycle breaking / deterministic free in tests; typed GDScript classes (no `-> void` on kernel callables): LOW
- Godot Physics 2D (no determinism claim; VS projection only, not MVP): LOW (Jolt default is 3D only)
- MultiplayerAPI / peer_id semantics (VS-B, MIRROR mode, no networking at MVP): MEDIUM, dormant

- Owner callable contract: `validate(cmd, views, ctx)`, `apply(cmd, write_scope, ctx)`, `snapshot(ctx)`, `restore(data, stored_version, ctx)`, `default_state(ctx)`, `post_restore(ctx)`, `read_view(ctx)`, `commit_baseline(ctx)`, `snap_baseline(key, ctx)`, `init_world(world_seed, ctx)`, `binding_source(ctx)`; ctx API `ok()`, `reject(reason)`, `put(payload)`, `fault(code, detail)`, `complete()`; contexts `ApplyContext`/`WriteScope`, `HookContext`, `SnapshotContext`, `NotifyContext`; `CompletionToken`

## Consumes

- Engine `_process(delta)` via the single TickDriver node (only wall-clock read, plus diagnostics timer); optional Godot Physics 2D observations in Vertical Slice (as inputs, PROJECTOR)
- Save/Load & Versioned Format: supplies `restore_epoch` (`slot_epoch.bin`), calls control plane, owns file I/O and `hex64`; kernel has no upstream game-system dependencies
- Owner-published callables from registrants: Life-Support Graph (`graph.state`, chained propagate hooks, pure join-validation query, `read_view.failures()`), Ship Body (`body.state`, `body.integrate` hook, `seat_bindings()`), Emitter State (`emitter.state`, `beam_bindings()`), Ship Section & Layout (`layout.state`, `block_hash(&"layout.state")`), Web Map & Transit (`init_world`, `pod_*` commands), Suit, Attention, Horror, Sanity (SIM level vs PERCEPTION_OUT), Modular Ship Assembly, Interaction, Player Controller (`loco_state`)
- Consumers that subscribe: Perception Filter, Debug Overlay, HUD, Lighting, Failure & Trail, Instruments, Adaptive Audio, Chart Table, Pixel-Perfect pipeline (read-only except INPUT_SURFACE submitters)

## Engine risk

- `Node._process` ordering, `process_priority`, `PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS` between nodes: LOW (reference silent on cross-node ordering; GDD says verify in spike, KRN-LAT-02)
- `Engine.time_scale` effect on `_process(delta)`: LOW but flagged [UNV] in GDD; verify in spike
- `Callable.call()` with typed return and completion-token identity pattern (GDScript has no try/catch; `assert` compiled out in release): LOW (older), must be exercised on release export (KRN-CTX-06)
- `var_to_bytes(..., false)` / `bytes_to_var` round-trip, Packed*Array pass-by-reference, `duplicate_deep()`: MEDIUM (`duplicate_deep` is 4.5+: HIGH)
- 4.7 behavior change: writing one element of a packed array no longer fires the property setter, so dirty tracking must be explicit in mutators: HIGH
- `HashingContext` SHA-256 over raw Packed bytes (H64): LOW
- `RefCounted` cycle breaking / deterministic free in tests; typed GDScript classes (no `-> void` on kernel callables): LOW
- Godot Physics 2D (no determinism claim; VS projection only, not MVP): LOW (Jolt default is 3D only)
- MultiplayerAPI / peer_id semantics (VS-B, MIRROR mode, no networking at MVP): MEDIUM, dormant
